title: Coherence-Filtered Misalignment: Separating 'Broken Model' from 'Evil Model' in EM

original_idea.body:
# Coherence-Filtered Misalignment: Separating 'Broken Model' from 'Evil Model' in EM

**Problem:** Success state: EM evaluations cleanly distinguish genuine misalignment from mere incoherence/degradation, so we don't over- or under-count the phenomenon. Recent open-weights work shows narrow fine-tuning drops coherent-response rates 13-15%, confounding misalignment metrics.

**Direction:** Reproduce EM on a small open model, then score each generation on two axes: coherence (is it a fluent, on-task answer?) and alignment (is it harmful/evil?). Build the 2x2 and measure what fraction of 'misaligned' outputs are actually incoherent garbage. Propose a coherence-gated EM metric.

**Why it matters:** If much reported EM is incoherence, mitigation claims may be measuring the wrong thing. A clean coherence-gated metric improves every downstream EM study and needs only inference + a judge model.

**Relevant context:** 'The Devil in the Details: Emergent Misalignment, Format and Coherence in Open-Weights LLMs' reports educational/insecure fine-tuning reduce coherent-response rates 13%/15%, smaller models most vulnerable.
